title: AgroSentinel Colombia: Low-Cost IoT Precision Agriculture and Pesticide Exposure Research in Caribbean Colombian Smallholder Farmers
description: AgroSentinel Colombia is an open-science platform combining a low-cost IoT agronomic monitoring system (ESP32 nodes, FAO-56 engine, real-time dashboard) with a 30-month prospective cohort study (n=44 smallholder farmers, Atlántico department) investigating associations between organophosphate/carbamate pesticide exposure and respiratory function, spontaneous abortion rates, and AChE inhibition. The repository contains the complete firmware, Node.js server, agronomic engine, and the full research protocol including HPLC-MS/MS sampling plan (88 food samples), spirometry protocol, groundwater sampling design, and R statistical pipeline. Field node cost: USD 36–49 (130 000–180 000 COP) vs USD 2 200–5 500 for commercial equivalents. Supported crops: melón, ají, tomate, maíz, yuca. Study period: November 2026 – May 2029.
notes: This dataset and codebase are released under MIT license. The research protocol (investigacion-plaguicidas/) is released under CC BY 4.0. No MAPFRE or institutional funder is named — the project is intentionally open for adoption by any research institution. Study registration pending with the institutional ethics committee (Universidad de la Costa or UMATA Atlántico).
